::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Sept 27th [1869]  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Princeton University, Parrish Collection, CO171: Box 29[^1]
:::

My dear [Mrs Johns](people/person_772.qmd),
Thank you for your kind invitation but I never know how to get out early enough for a one o’clock luncheon. [Helen](people/person_1613.qmd)’s lessons last me till half past eleven, and if I do not work from that time till two, I can get nothing done, and as I am going from home the week after next, I am more hurried than is convenient, so that I cannot well spare the morning hours. I will bring in some spare [M P](organizations/other_52.qmd)s with the story and hope to appear between half past three and four on Saturday.[^2]

If it were not for more than usual work, I would gladly come to your early dinner.

I will send the papers to [Miss Sewell](people/person_1301.qmd). With many thanks
Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Black-edged paper.
[^2]: It is uncertain which story is referred to here.
